title: Technology Sector Update for 07/03/2018: VEON,ACXM,IPG,RAMP,ATEN,TRMB
text:

Tech stocks were sharply lower late in Tuesday's holiday-shortened session, with shares of technology companies in the S&P 500 index falling over 0.8% in the afternoon while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was nearly 1.3% lower.
Among technology stocks likely moving on news:
+ Veon ( VEON ) rallied Tuesday, jumping as much as 26% higher, after a Hong Kong-based conglomerate agreed to buy out the Dutch mobile carrier's stake in an Italian mobile-phone joint venture, for EUR2.45 billion, or about $2.9 billion. In a statement, CK Hutchison early Tuesday said it was acquiring VEON's 50% stake in the privately held Wind Tre, making the Asian telecom giant the sole owner of their former joint venture. The deal is subject to European Union and Italian regulatory approvals and should close during Q3 or Q4, Veon said, adding it expects to use a "fraction" of the sale proceeds to buy the assets of Global Telecom Holding in Pakistan and Bangladesh. Remaining funds will be to pay down debt. The upcoming sale also prompted analysts at JPMorgan to raise their investment rating for Veon shares to Overweight from Neutral.
In other sector news:
+ Acxiom ( ACXM ) opened Tuesday at a four-year high, rising over 9% to its best share price since February 2014 at $37.38 apiece and since climbing as high as $39.57 a share after the marketing technology company agreed to sell its Acxiom Marketing Solutions business to the Interpublic Group ( IPG ) for $2.3 billion in cash. Acxiom plans to use a portion of the $1.7 billion in net proceeds from the deal to retire all of its outstanding $230 million in debt in addition to launching a cash tender offer for up to $500 million of its common stock and extending the program through the end of 2020. It also will transfer the Acxiom brand name and associated trademarks to IPG and rename the remaining assets as LiveRamp and shortly thereafter begin trading its common stock under the RAMP ticker symbol.
+ A10 Networks ( ATEN ) rose as much as 5% on Tuesday after late Monday saying its financial statements dating back to September 2016 should be restated, although it also said the errors are unlikely to change the total amount of revenue it recognized over that period. The errors were uncovered during an internal probe, the company said, adding it expects to shift the timing of when some of that revenue was recognized. Revenue for the 12 months ended Dec. 31, 2016, was overstated by around $3 million, it said, including about $1 million in overstated revenue during the three months ended Sept. 30, 2016, while its FY17 net loss was understated by about a net $2 million error and included a $1 million Q1 understatement and a $3 million Q3 overstatement.
Trimble ( TRMB ) was narrowly higher on Tuesday, easing from a nearly 1% gain earlier in the session that followed the company saying it has completed its purchase of Viewpoint from Bain Capital, paying $1.2 billion in cash for the job-site and field software firm. The companies announced the acquisition of Viewpoint in April and Trimble funded the deal with a combination of senior notes, a term loan and other existing credit facilities along with cash on hand.
